engines.B: second engine, independent of the first, full-resolution page image

method: page-local: the cleaned verse text, reduced to lowercase letters and digits, must occur inside the reduced whole-page reading B of the same PDF page (print_match true/false; null = no text in the scan). Agreement is not a print check: both engines read the same pixels.

clean_rules.R1: join the verse's OCR lines with one space
clean_rules.R2: map ligature/long-s code points (ff fi fl ffi ffl, long s) to plain letters
clean_rules.R3: line-end hyphen: keep it if the hyphenated compound occurs in-line elsewhere in the book; else join the halves if the joined word occurs whole elsewhere in the book or in the system word list; else keep it if both halves are words; else join (every decision logged per row)
clean_rules.R4: remove footnote-reference marks the OCR rendered as symbols: a trailing run of *, dagger, registered/degree signs or superscript digits glued after final punctuation, a glued trailing 't' (dagger misread) after final punctuation, and * or superscript glyphs inside a word (mid-word marks become a space)
clean_rules.R6: spacing: where two engines read the same letters with different word breaks, take the reading whose words are all in the vocabulary (system word list plus words the book itself uses 3+ times)
clean_rules.R7: letter majority: where readings A and B differ in letters and reading C equals reading B, take that token (2 of 3 readings)
clean_rules.R10: run-together words: a token that is not a word but segments uniquely into very common words of the book (15+ occurrences each), all function words (it/is/to/of/if...) except at most one longer word, is split at those boundaries (logged per row)
clean_rules.R9: lexical tie-break: where the readings differ in letters and exactly one candidate is a vocabulary word (word, or word minus a common/archaic suffix), take it; if both or neither are words the row goes to a ruling
clean_rules.R11: final mark: where reading A ends in , ; or : and reading B, on the same verse and otherwise the same punctuation, ends in . ? or !, take reading B's mark (a choice between two readings, never a typed mark)
clean_rules.R12: punctuation kept by majority: where readings A and B differ in punctuation, reading A's marks are kept only if 3 of the 5 readings (A, B, C, B on a half-resolution copy, B on a 1.5x copy) carry them
clean_rules.R13: specks: a period that is an isolated token or sits before a lower-case word is dropped only if that makes reading A's punctuation equal to all three readings by the second engine (which agree with each other)
clean_rules.R20: symbols: characters other than letters, spaces and . , : ; ! ? ' ’ - ( ) removed, each logged
clean_rules.R21: spelling: a word not in the vocabulary replaced by the aligned word of another reading that is
clean_rules.R22: spelling: a word not in the vocabulary replaced by the single vocabulary word one letter edit away (dictionary correction)
clean_rules.R23: spelling: a word not in the vocabulary that splits into two vocabulary words (one a function word) is split
clean_rules.R24: final mark: reading B's . ? or !, else the first of readings A and C that ends in one
clean_rules.R25: spelling: where two readings' words are both vocabulary words, the one 10x more frequent in the corpus wins if two other readings carry it
clean_rules.R29: apostrophe specks: an apostrophe inside a word that readings A and C both read without one (same letters) is dropped, unless it is a possessive or contraction ending ('s 'd 't 'st 'll 're 've)
clean_rules.R27: hyphen specks: a hyphenated token in reading B whose two halves readings A and C both read as two separate words is split at the hyphen
clean_rules.R28: final mark: the mark given by a ruling made from the page image replaces whatever the readings ended in
clean_rules.R30: typed edition: this text's word is not a word (or unattested in Pope/Drew while the epub's occurs 30+ times) and the epub's aligned word is: take the epub's word, keep this text's marks
clean_rules.R31: typed edition: the epub has words this text lacks (a lost word, including the verse's last word): insert them; a dash speck before them and a premature final mark are dropped
clean_rules.R32: typed edition: an extra token in this text is not a word (a speck such as ':T') and the epub lacks it: drop it
clean_rules.R33: typed edition: a '.' in this text (or ':' after a function word) before a lower-case word, which the epub lacks, is a speck: drop the mark
clean_rules.R34: typed edition: a run-together token in this text has the same letters as the epub's separate words, which are words: take the epub's spacing
clean_rules.R35: typed edition: both are words but this text's is common in Pope/Drew and the epub's is unattested or 10x rarer: a typing slip in the epub; this text's word stays (logged, no change)
clean_rules.R37: typed edition: this text has no final mark, its letters equal the epub's and the epub ends in . ? or !: take its mark
clean_rules.R36: typed edition: a ruling on a difference no rule could settle (A this text, B the epub's word(s), T a text typed from the page)
clean_rules.R26: semicolons: where readings A and C both carry ';' at the same position and reading B has ':', the ';' stands (reading B gave 0 of 2 printed semicolons in verses typed from the page)
clean_rules.R8: drop isolated stray symbol tokens (| _ < > { } [ ] / \ ~ * dagger) that carry no letter or digit
